transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific that’s been bothering you or that you’d like to talk about?

I came in because ever since my wife’s fall, I just haven’t been myself. I used to be the one with the lists and the plan, keeping everything in order, and now I sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart and just… freeze. I’ll cry, or snap over nothing. Bills are piling up, I’ve missed mentoring calls, and even basic housework feels like something I can’t make myself do. It’s like I’m not functioning the way I used to.
How long ago did your wife’s fall happen, and have you noticed your symptoms improving at all since then, or have they stayed the same?
It happened about two months ago. Since then, things have really stayed pretty much the same—maybe up and down day to day, but overall I don’t feel like I’ve improved.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, like hobbies or time with friends or family?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying much attention to hobbies or seeing people lately, so I can’t say clearly whether I’m enjoying them less. It’s just been hard to think beyond what’s right in front of me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your wife’s fall?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve definitely felt overwhelmed and not like myself, but I haven’t really been tracking it that way.
Have you noticed that you’re not interested in things you used to enjoy, or that you don’t get as much pleasure out of them as you did before your wife’s fall?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been doing much of the things I used to enjoy lately, so it’s hard to tell if I’m not interested or if I’m just not getting to them. I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly one way or the other.
Have you noticed that you’re not interested in things you used to enjoy, or that you don’t get as much pleasure out of them as you did before your wife’s fall?
I don’t really have a clear answer. I haven’t been keeping up with those things enough to know if I’m enjoying them less, or if I’m just too caught up in everything to notice.
Have you noticed any change in how you feel about activities you used to enjoy, like whether you still look forward to them or not?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been thinking ahead to those things or making plans for them, so I can’t say if I still look forward to them the same way or not.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or that they don’t bring you the same pleasure as before your wife’s fall?
I honestly can’t say for sure. I haven’t really been doing those things enough to know whether I’ve lost interest or if I’d still enjoy them if I tried. It’s just been hard to tell.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or that they don’t bring you the same pleasure as before your wife’s fall?

I guess I still don’t know how to answer that clearly. I haven’t really gone back to those things enough to judge. Right now everything’s been so tied up with my wife’s situation that I can’t tell if the enjoyment is gone, or if I just haven’t had the space for it.
Looking back, have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends or family, have become less interesting or less enjoyable since your wife’s fall?

I don’t really know. I haven’t been doing much of those things lately, so it’s hard for me to tell whether they’re less enjoyable or if I just haven’t had the chance to get into them. Since her fall, my attention’s been mostly on that.
Looking back, can you recall if there was a time in the past two months when you genuinely looked forward to or enjoyed something, even briefly?
I’m not sure I can point to a clear moment like that. Maybe there were small things, but nothing really stands out to me as something I genuinely looked forward to or enjoyed. It’s been hard to tell.
Can you think of any activity, even small ones like watching a show or taking a walk, that you’ve felt even a little interested in or got some pleasure from in the past two months?

I honestly can’t think of anything specific. I mean, I might put the TV on or step outside, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really felt interested in it or gotten pleasure from it in a way that stands out. It’s more like I’m just getting through the day.

Can you describe how you’ve been feeling emotionally, beyond just being overwhelmed? Has there been a general mood, like sadness or hopelessness, that’s been with you most days since your wife’s fall?

Yes. Since my wife’s fall, I feel like I’ve just... changed. I used to be the person with the lists and the plan, keeping things moving. Now I sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart, and I’ll start crying, or I’ll snap over something small.

It’s not just feeling busy or stressed. I feel worn down most days, like I can’t get myself to function the way I normally would. Bills pile up, calls I’m supposed to make pile up, even basic housework piles up. I wouldn’t say I have a neat word for it, but emotionally it’s been heavy and out of control.
Have you noticed that you’ve been lacking energy or feeling slowed down most days since your wife’s fall?

Yes, most days I feel like I’m moving through mud. Since my wife’s fall, I’ve gone from being the person who had lists and a plan to just sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I’ll cry, or snap over something small, and then the bills, calls I’m supposed to make, even basic housework just pile up because I can’t seem to get myself going.
Looking back over the past two months, have you experienced any days where you felt a clear sense of hopelessness or felt that life wasn’t worth living?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I’ve felt pretty low and worn out, but I can’t point to a clear day where I thought life wasn’t worth living. Hopeless… maybe discouraged at times, but I don’t know that I’ve had that specific feeling clearly.
Looking back over the past two months, would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to care about or that nothing has been able to give you even a little pleasure?

I don’t think I’d say it’s been completely gone, no. I haven’t really paid close attention to it that way. A lot of things feel harder to enjoy right now, but I can’t honestly say nothing gives me even a little pleasure.
Would you say that your mood has been low or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, since your wife’s fall?

Yes… most days since her fall, I’ve been very low. I used to be the one with lists and a plan, and now I end up sitting at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart, crying or snapping over nothing. It’s like I just can’t make myself function the way I used to.
